title: Implement GraphQL Subscriptions over WebSockets for Real-Time Updates
description: The PulseStream Showtime API currently supports GraphQL queries and mutations, primarily handled via standard HTTP requests and a basic WebSocket channel for query execution. To enhance user experience, we need to implement GraphQL Subscriptions to provide clients with real-time updates. This is a large feature that will be developed over multiple sessions. The first session focuses on laying the architectural groundwork. The core task involves integrating with the existing WebSocket handler (`websocket_handler.c`), the GraphQL execution engine (`graphql_executor.c`), and the publish-subscribe system (`event_bus.c`) to enable persistent, event-driven communication.

project_spec.name: PulseStream Showtime API
project_spec.description:
PulseStream Showtime API exposes a real-time catalog and interaction layer for live concerts, e-sports broadcasts, and interactive talk shows. Instead of a traditional request/response backend, every user action—ticket purchase, vote, chat reaction, backstage access request—emits domain events that flow through an internal event bus. Dedicated service handlers turn those events into GraphQL-ready materialized views, so mobile apps, smart TVs, and AR headsets can subscribe to fresh entertainment data with millisecond latency.   

The project ships an API Gateway combining REST onboarding endpoints with a single GraphQL schema. Features such as rate-limiting, JWT-based authentication, cursor-based pagination, and response caching are handled at the gateway layer, while a service layer written in C processes events, validates incoming mutations, logs structured traces, and publishes change notifications. All endpoints are self-documented through an OpenAPI sidecar and GraphQL SDL comments, ensuring smooth integration for third-party game studios and streaming partners.
dependencies: libmicrohttpd (lightweight HTTP server for REST/GraphQL gateway)
libuv (cross-platform event loop underpinning the event bus)
cJSON (fast JSON generation for responses and caching)
hiredis (Redis client used for response caching & rate-limiting counters)
libcurl (outbound webhooks to external streaming services)
nanomsg (in-process pub/sub between internal service modules)
